summary: Define two fixed stock concentrations for one reagent using the established two-stock allocation, calibration and printing workflow.
notes: Enter two positive finite concentrations separated by a comma, for example 5, 500. The exact pair overrides the automatic two-stock checkbox, and both stocks remain present even when one is unused. Concentrations must have distinct stock identities at two decimal places.

Fixed-pair allocation uses the existing nearest-achievable two-stock solver and volume checks. Saving, editable copies, calibration and saved-progress resume preserve the pair. Invalid input retains the last valid result.

Includes the Windows development-worktree tooling and offline-analysis CLI import correction already on main. Runtime dependencies, machine-data schema, execution-calibration version 4 and execution-data capabilities are unchanged.

The tracked firmware artifact differs from v1.3.0 only in eight build date/time bytes. No firmware runtime source, configuration or wire-protocol change accompanies this feature. The changed artifact is explicitly declared above; application updating does not itself establish installed firmware readiness.

Retains the exact v1.2.0-rc.6, v1.2.0 and v1.3.0-rc.1 stable migration cohorts and the separate pinned rc.11 release-candidate route. Direct legacy deployment still requires the established guarded migration, firmware/recovery verification and attended first-machine canary.

No historical app rollback is configured or qualified for this release. Preserve calibration measurements, committed counts, immutable revisions and progress; use protected current-version or exactly qualified compatible-bundle recovery. Older designers do not support the new fixed-pair constraint.

The attended Pi operator confirmed fixed-pair calibration, printing and resume. This does not add long-session memory, historical-recording replay or optimizer timing qualification; existing accepted large-optimizer UI-pause limitations remain. See docs/v1.3.1_release_qualification.md.
